concepts.title: Nouns and Pronouns
concepts.description: Nouns and Pronouns — part of the chapter on Parts of Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of nouns and pronouns
Step-by-step problem solving for nouns and pronouns
Real-world applications of nouns and pronouns

concepts.title: Verbs and Tenses
concepts.description: Verbs and Tenses — part of the chapter on Parts of Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of verbs and tenses
Step-by-step problem solving for verbs and tenses
Real-world applications of verbs and tenses

concepts.title: Adjectives and Adverbs
concepts.description: Explores modifiers that describe, qualify, or limit nouns and verbs, including the rules for comparative and superlative forms.
key_ideas: Adjectives modify nouns and pronouns by answering 'what kind', 'which one', or 'how many'
Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, often ending in -ly
Distinguishing between adjectives and adverbs in sentence construction
Formation and usage of comparative and superlative degrees

concepts.title: Articles and Determiners
concepts.description: Focuses on the specific class of words used to introduce nouns and specify their reference, quantity, or possession.
key_ideas: Definite (the) vs. Indefinite (a/an) articles
Demonstratives (this, that, these, those)
Quantifiers (some, many, few) and their agreement with countable/uncountable nouns
Possessive determiners (my, your, his, her)

concepts.title: Prepositions and Spatial Relationships
concepts.description: Examines words that show the relationship between a noun or pronoun and other words in a sentence, focusing on location, direction, and time.
key_ideas: Common prepositions of place, time, and movement
Identifying the object of the preposition
Constructing and placing prepositional phrases within sentences
Distinguishing prepositions from particles in phrasal verbs

concepts.title: Conjunctions and Interjections
concepts.description: Covers the words used to connect clauses or sentences and words used to express independent emotion.
key_ideas: Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS) for joining equal parts
Subordinating conjunctions for dependent clauses
Correlative conjunctions (either/or, neither/nor)
Usage and punctuation of interjections for emotional emphasis

concepts.title: Functional Analysis of Parts of Speech
concepts.description: Advanced identification of word classes based on their syntactic function within specific contexts rather than memorized definitions.
key_ideas: Words functioning as multiple parts of speech (e.g., 'run' as noun vs. verb)
Contextual clues for identifying word class
The impact of shifting parts of speech on sentence meaning
Analyzing complex sentences for grammatical agreement

concepts.title: Simple, Compound and Complex Sentences
concepts.description: Simple, Compound and Complex Sentences — part of the chapter on Sentence Structure.
key_ideas: Core principles of simple, compound and complex sentences
Step-by-step problem solving for simple, compound and complex sentences
Real-world applications of simple, compound and complex sentences

concepts.title: Subject and Predicate Basics
concepts.description: Explores the two fundamental parts of every complete sentence: the subject (who or what the sentence is about) and the predicate (what is said about the subject).
key_ideas: Distinguishing between simple subjects and complete subjects
Identifying simple and compound predicates
Recognizing the implied 'you' in imperative sentences

concepts.title: Clauses vs. Phrases
concepts.description: Differentiates between phrases (groups of words without a subject-verb pair) and clauses (groups of words containing both), and distinguishes independent from dependent clauses.
key_ideas: Identifying independent clauses as complete thoughts
Recognizing dependent (subordinate) clauses and their markers
The role of prepositional and appositive phrases in structure

concepts.title: Sentence Fragments and Run-ons
concepts.description: Focuses on identifying and correcting common structural errors, specifically incomplete sentences (fragments) and improperly joined sentences (run-ons and comma splices).
key_ideas: Fixing fragments by attaching them to main clauses or adding missing components
Identifying comma splices where two independent clauses are joined only by a comma
Correcting fused sentences using periods, semicolons, or conjunctions

concepts.title: The Compound-Complex Sentence
concepts.description: An advanced structural form that combines the characteristics of both compound and complex sentences to express nuanced relationships between multiple ideas.
key_ideas: Structure: At least two independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses
Using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions simultaneously
Managing punctuation in long, multi-clause sentences

concepts.title: Parallel Structure
concepts.description: Teaches the importance of using the same grammatical form for items in a list or comparison to create balance, rhythm, and clarity in writing.
key_ideas: Balancing verb tenses and forms (e.g., gerunds vs. infinitives) in lists
Using parallel structure with correlative conjunctions (either/or, neither/nor)
Enhancing readability and style through grammatical symmetry

concepts.title: Present, Past and Future — Simple, Continuous, Perfect
concepts.description: Present, Past and Future — Simple, Continuous, Perfect — part of the chapter on Tenses.
key_ideas: Core principles of present, past and future
Step-by-step problem solving for present, past and future
Real-world applications of present, past and future

concepts.title: Stative vs. Dynamic Verbs
concepts.description: Differentiation between action verbs (dynamic) and state verbs (stative) to prevent misuse in continuous tenses.
key_ideas: Definition of stative verbs (thoughts, emotions, senses, possession)
The rule: Stative verbs generally cannot be used in continuous forms
Verbs with dual meanings (e.g., 'to have' as possession vs. action)
Common errors like 'I am liking this'

concepts.title: Future Forms: Will, Going To, and Present Continuous
concepts.description: A deep dive into the specific contexts required for different future forms beyond the simple usage of 'will'.
key_ideas: Using 'Will' for spontaneous decisions and predictions
Using 'Going to' for prior intentions and evidence-based predictions
Using Present Continuous for fixed arrangements and scheduled plans
Using Present Simple for timetables (e.g., trains, flights)

concepts.title: The Perfect Continuous Aspect
concepts.description: Mastering the Present, Past, and Future Perfect Continuous tenses to express duration and ongoing actions relative to a time reference.
key_ideas: Emphasis on the duration of an activity rather than the result
Using 'for' and 'since' with continuous forms
Distinguishing Present Perfect Simple (completion) vs. Present Perfect Continuous (ongoing/recent activity)
Past Perfect Continuous for causes of past states

concepts.title: Expressing Past Habits: Used to vs. Would
concepts.description: Techniques for describing discontinued habits and states in the past without using the Past Simple tense.
key_ideas: Structure and usage of 'used to' for past states and actions
Usage of 'would' specifically for repeated past actions (nostalgia)
The constraint: 'Would' cannot be used for past states
Difference between 'used to do' and 'be/get used to doing'

concepts.title: Narrative Tenses and Sequencing
concepts.description: Synthesizing multiple past tenses to construct coherent stories with clear timelines and background context.
key_ideas: Using Past Simple for the main events/timeline
Using Past Continuous for setting the scene or interrupted actions
Using Past Perfect to sequence events that happened before the main narrative time
Managing time shifts in complex storytelling

concepts.title: Active and Passive Voice
concepts.description: Active and Passive Voice — part of the chapter on Active-Passive Voice and Direct-Indirect Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of active and passive voice
Step-by-step problem solving for active and passive voice
Real-world applications of active and passive voice

concepts.title: Direct and Indirect Speech
concepts.description: Direct and Indirect Speech — part of the chapter on Active-Passive Voice and Direct-Indirect Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of direct and indirect speech
Step-by-step problem solving for direct and indirect speech
Real-world applications of direct and indirect speech

concepts.title: Tense Transformation Rules in Passive Voice
concepts.description: A detailed breakdown of how auxiliary verbs change across different tenses (Simple, Continuous, Perfect) when converting from active to passive voice.
key_ideas: Insertion of 'being' for continuous tenses
Insertion of 'been' for perfect tenses
Handling modal verbs (can, should, must) in passive constructions
Tenses that do not have a standard passive form (e.g., Future Continuous)

concepts.title: Interrogative Sentences in Passive Voice
concepts.description: Techniques for converting questions from active to passive voice, focusing on the placement of auxiliary verbs and the transformation of question words.
key_ideas: Converting 'Who' to 'By whom'
Maintaining question structure (auxiliary before subject) in passive voice
Handling Yes/No questions in passive transformations
Positioning of prepositions in interrogative passive sentences

concepts.title: Tense Backshifting in Indirect Speech
concepts.description: The rules governing the shift of tenses from present to past, or past to past perfect, when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
key_ideas: Simple Present becomes Simple Past
Present Perfect becomes Past Perfect
Exceptions to backshifting (universal truths and habitual facts)
Changes in time and place expressions (e.g., 'now' becomes 'then', 'here' becomes 'there')

concepts.title: Reporting Questions in Indirect Speech
concepts.description: Methods for converting direct questions into indirect speech, distinguishing between Wh- questions and Yes/No questions.
key_ideas: Using 'if' or 'whether' for Yes/No questions
Retaining the question word for Wh- questions
Changing interrogative word order to statement word order (removing inversion)
Removing the question mark in reported speech

concepts.title: Reporting Imperatives and Exclamations
concepts.description: Strategies for converting commands, requests, advice, and exclamations into indirect speech by altering the reporting verb and sentence structure.
key_ideas: Changing the reporting verb to reflect tone (ordered, requested, exclaimed)
Converting imperatives into infinitive phrases (to + verb)
Handling negative commands (not to + verb)
Transforming exclamatory sentences into assertive statements

concepts.title: Unseen Passages and Note Making
concepts.description: Unseen Passages and Note Making — part of the chapter on Reading Comprehension.
key_ideas: Core principles of unseen passages and note making
Step-by-step problem solving for unseen passages and note making
Real-world applications of unseen passages and note making

concepts.title: Skimming and Scanning Strategies
concepts.description: Techniques for rapid reading to grasp the general gist of a text or locate specific information quickly without reading every word.
key_ideas: Skimming for the main idea or gist
Scanning for specific keywords, dates, or names
Reading headings, subheadings, and topic sentences
Time management during reading assessments

concepts.title: Identifying Main Ideas and Supporting Details
concepts.description: The ability to distinguish the primary argument or central theme of a paragraph from the examples, evidence, and elaboration that support it.
key_ideas: Locating topic sentences
Distinguishing between core themes and minor details
Understanding paragraph structure
Summarizing the central message

concepts.title: Vocabulary in Context
concepts.description: Strategies for determining the meaning of unfamiliar words or phrases by analyzing the surrounding text rather than relying on a dictionary.
key_ideas: Using synonyms and antonyms provided in the text
Analyzing semantic logic and sentence structure
Identifying roots and affixes for clues
Understanding idiomatic expressions within context

concepts.title: Inference, Tone, and Mood
concepts.description: Reading between the lines to understand implied meanings, the author's attitude, and the emotional atmosphere of the text.
key_ideas: Deducing implicit information not stated directly
Identifying the author's tone (e.g., sarcastic, objective, critical)
Recognizing the mood or atmosphere of a narrative
Drawing logical conclusions based on evidence

concepts.title: Critical Evaluation: Fact, Opinion, and Bias
concepts.description: Advanced comprehension skills focused on assessing the validity of arguments, distinguishing objective facts from subjective opinions, and detecting authorial bias.
key_ideas: Differentiating between verifiable facts and personal opinions
Identifying author bias or underlying agenda
Evaluating the strength and relevance of arguments
Recognizing logical fallacies in persuasive texts

concepts.title: Letter, Essay and Article Writing
concepts.description: Letter, Essay and Article Writing — part of the chapter on Writing Skills.
key_ideas: Core principles of letter, essay and article writing
Step-by-step problem solving for letter, essay and article writing
Real-world applications of letter, essay and article writing

concepts.title: Paragraph Structure and Development
concepts.description: The fundamental building blocks of writing, focusing on creating unified and coherent paragraphs with a clear focus.
key_ideas: Crafting effective topic sentences
Using supporting details and evidence
Writing concluding sentences
Maintaining unity within a paragraph

concepts.title: Cohesion and Coherence
concepts.description: Techniques to ensure logical flow and connection between ideas, sentences, and paragraphs.
key_ideas: Using transitional words and phrases
Reference and substitution
Logical sequencing of ideas
Avoiding disjointed writing

concepts.title: Precis and Summary Writing
concepts.description: The skill of condensing a larger text into a concise summary while retaining the essential core meaning and tone.
key_ideas: Identifying main vs. subordinate ideas
Paraphrasing techniques
Maintaining the original author's perspective
Brevity and conciseness rules

concepts.title: Story and Narrative Writing
concepts.description: Developing creative narratives that engage readers through structured storytelling elements.
key_ideas: Developing plot structure (exposition, climax, resolution)
Character development and dialogue
Setting the scene and atmosphere
Using descriptive imagery

concepts.title: Report Writing
concepts.description: Drafting formal, objective accounts of events, investigations, or newspaper reports following specific structural conventions.
key_ideas: Structure of a report (headline, byline, lead paragraph)
Using objective and formal language
Presenting facts and data clearly
Difference between newspaper and business reports
